issues: No correctness issues found. Re-ran the driver end-to-end (629.7s, exit 0): every reported figure reproduced bit-for-bit (MEAN/P90/P95 levels with identical CIs; savings +0.0615/+0.1762/+0.1148 with identical CIs; min/max; def_rate=1.0 for all three; control cost 1.311544 == deterministic). Checked the three flagged bug classes specifically and all are clear: (1) the control is NOT vacuous - zero-spread stochastic collapses 3 identical p50 paths under the 'shared' binary to the deterministic p50 controller, a genuine scenario-coupling integrity check that would catch band-collapse / 1-vs-3 alternate-optima bugs; (2) no hidden baseline duplication - naive (half=0, p50), Phase1 (half=0, center=0.8*p50+0.2*p10), Phase2 (3 spread paths) feed genuinely distinct planner inputs and yield distinct outputs; (3) monotonicity naive>phase1>phase2 is plausible not implausible - identical min costs (0.2196 sunny days where battery trivially covers load) with differentiation appearing in mean+tail is exactly the expected signature of progressively better hedging. Statistics are sound: difference CIs use correct PAIRED bootstrap (shared resample indices across controllers, justified since one PV draw drives all three each day), and the SOLID verdicts rest on those paired difference CIs excluding zero - NOT on the overlapping marginal level CIs. Only nit: runtime 630s slightly over the 6-min guideline (env/solver overhead, not a correctness concern), already disclosed by the prior agent.
final_takeaways: VERIFIED by re-run (bit-for-bit reproduction, seed-fixed deterministic). Phase2 (3-scenario stochastic MPC) beats naive by +0.176 AUD/day mean; paired bootstrap 90% CI [+0.149,+0.205] excludes zero -> SOLID. Phase1 (P10-bias b=0.20 deterministic) beats naive by +0.062/day, CI [+0.054,+0.070] -> SOLID.

Phase2 beats Phase1 by +0.115/day, 90% CI [+0.093,+0.137] -> SOLID. The full three-scenario recourse LP recovers meaningfully more value than the scalar P10-bias heuristic at aft_sd=0.3. The paired-difference test is the correct one here; the marginal level CIs overlap but that does NOT weaken the conclusion.

Tail-risk reduction is the headline and is statistically supported (P90/P95 each have their own bootstrap CIs that order cleanly): Phase2 P95 3.33 vs naive 4.09 (~18% lower worst-case spend), P90 3.07 vs 3.68 (~17% lower). Phase1 trims the tail less (P95 3.89). This matches the expected signature of stochastic hedging against bad afternoon-PV realizations.

The control is a real formulation-integrity check, not a rubber stamp: collapsing the forecast bands to zero makes the 3-scenario LP identical to the deterministic P50 baseline (cost 1.311544, diff 0.00, done=4 both). This is the exact class of test that previously caught band-collapse and scenario-coupling bugs.
Worst-day (max) values (naive 4.72 / phase1 4.29 / phase2 3.77) are single realizations from 300 draws; the ordering is suggestive but NOT confirmed by CI - treat as illustrative only.
Deferrable completion is 100% for all three controllers across all 300 days, confirming the carryover mechanism is robust under aft_sd=0.3.

Absolute AUD/day figures come from a stylized 8 kWh / 4 kW single-household model with synthetic Australian-style tariffs and a simple additive-Gaussian afternoon-uncertainty model (no skew, no spatial correlation). Rankings and ratios are the load-bearing results, not the absolute dollar values.
